scenes.headline: What a 145B model on one GPU is made of
scenes.sub: Edge0-145B and 120B, read from their own files
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Corwin! Edge0 says this model runs on a laptop. I read every file header in the release to see what it is.

states.say: Start with a hundred and forty-five billion parameters, as the card counts them.

states.term: N-gram table: rows looked up by the last few tokens
states.say: Most are experts. A third is one lookup table, keyed by the last few tokens. The rest is attention, routers and projections.
Now sort them by where they live. The table never leaves the SSD. A token reads sixteen small rows of it.

left.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
left.say: The base is Qwen's Flash-Next. The routers I compared are byte-identical in Edge0's files, and the lookup table matches NVIDIA's copy of Qwen's.

right.title: Edge0-145B
right.say: What changed is the expert pool. Every expert is narrower, seventy percent of the size.

scenes.title: A latent in front of the experts

params.billDU: D and U: 73.4M a layer, every token

steps.say: In Qwen's layer, a token two thousand five hundred and sixty wide goes straight into ten of five hundred and twelve experts.

steps.term: Latent: a narrower width the experts work at
steps.say: Edge0 puts a shared projection in front, eight of them per layer. The experts now work seventeen ninety-two wide.
A second projection widens the result back. Attention never sees the difference.
The price. Those projections are seventy-three million weights a layer, read for every token. The ten experts that fire are thirty-four million.

scenes.title: One verify window, on one GPU

steps.say: So how does it run? A small draft layer guesses up to four tokens.
The full model checks them in one pass. Nine gigabytes of dense weights, read once.

steps.term: Verify window: one pass that checks several drafted tokens
steps.say: Plus two point four gigabytes of experts the four tokens route to.
The GPU computes the experts it caches. The CPU computes the rest where they sit, in RAM. The SSD only holds the table.
About three tokens kept per pass. On a twenty-four gigabyte card with sixty-four of RAM, that is around a hundred tokens a second.
Now the speed claim, from Edge0's own setup video.

steps.caption: 69 tokens of prompt, first token 1.2 s
steps.say: Sixty-nine tokens of prompt. Over a thousand a second of prefill, with a first token after one point two seconds. Fixed costs dominate a prompt that short.

scenes.title: RTX Spark N1X decode, tok/s
scenes.say: On that machine, the README's best row for the 145B is forty-six. The 120B reaches sixty-nine. And twelve-eighty is the 120B's latent width.

steps.say: Then memory. Both models are plotted at twenty-nine gigabytes.
Edge0 is measured internal peak.

steps.caption: Release's own reading: 54.4 GiB, every expert resident
steps.say: The release's own reading, with every expert in VRAM or RAM, is fifty-four gigabytes. Twenty-nine leaves most of the experts uncounted.

scenes.say: Edge0-145B is Qwen's model with narrower experts, run by Strata's engine on fifty-four gigabytes of VRAM and RAM. A good result. Not twenty-nine.
